description: The JSON shape of one Action, the mapping vocabulary stored per control in config.json (DESIGN v2.4 B, v2.7 A). Swift's synthesized enum Codable writes a case as an object with one key, the case name, whose value is an object: empty for a case without a payload, {"_0": prompt} for sendPrompt. expected is the exact compact text JSONEncoder writes with .sortedKeys (no spaces): the escapes are \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t and lowercase \u00xx for the other C0 controls; everything else, including DEL, U+2028 and non-ASCII, is written raw as UTF-8. Input is an action descriptor: {"case": <case name>} plus "prompt" for sendPrompt.
function: Action encoding — input an action descriptor, expected the compact JSON text of that one action
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.4 B and v2.7 A; Tests/PowerUpTests/MappingFixtureTests.swift testActionShapeTable encodes the action with JSONEncoder (.sortedKeys) and compares the bytes, and compares CoreBridge.wireJSON(of:) (the core, through the bridge) with them too. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/mapping.rs action_shape_matches_swift_bytes writes the action with Action::to_wire_json and compares the bytes, then reads the text back with serde_json::from_str::<Action>.

cases.name: sendPrompt with an empty prompt
cases.reason: An empty prompt is still a string payload, never an omitted _0.

cases.name: sendPrompt with CJK and emoji
cases.reason: Non-ASCII is written raw (UTF-8), not as \u escapes.

cases.name: sendPrompt with quotes and a backslash
cases.reason: Quote and backslash are the two characters every JSON writer must escape.

cases.name: sendPrompt with a newline and a tab
cases.reason: Short escapes \n and \t, never \u000a.

cases.name: sendPrompt with C0 controls
cases.reason: Other controls are \u00xx with lowercase hex.

cases.name: sendPrompt with backspace, form feed and CR
cases.reason: The remaining short escapes, as the Swift encoder writes them.

cases.name: sendPrompt with a slash
cases.reason: Swift's JSONEncoder writes / as \/; serde_json does not, so the Rust writer escapes it itself.

cases.name: sendPrompt with a line separator and DEL
cases.reason: U+2028 and DEL are written raw by Swift; escaping them would change the bytes.
